title: Crispy Pork Carnitas
cook: 8–10 hr on low or 5–6 hr on high, plus 5 min under the broiler
total: 8 hr 30 min–10 hr 30 min on low (5 hr 30 min–6 hr 30 min on high)

items: 3–4 lb boneless pork shoulder (pork butt), thick fat trimmed, cut into 3-inch chunks
1 medium yellow onion, sliced ½ inch thick
16 small corn or flour tortillas, warmed
½ small white onion, finely diced

steps: Mix the salt, cumin, oregano and chili powder in a small bowl. Rub it all over the pork chunks.
Spread the sliced onion and garlic in the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker and set the pork on top. Squeeze the orange and lime juice over the pork, then tuck the squeezed halves in around it.
Cover and cook on low 8–10 hr or on high 5–6 hr, until the pork falls apart when pressed with a fork. It will be well past the safe 145°F, around 195–205°F, which is what lets it shred.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Lift the pork onto a cutting board, throw away the citrus halves and shred the meat with two forks, pulling out any fatty bits.
Spread the pork in a single layer on a rimmed sheet pan and spoon ½ cup of the cooking juices over it.
Broil 3–5 min, until the edges are brown and crisp. Watch closely after 3 min. Stir and broil 2 min more if you want extra crispy bits.
Serve in warm tortillas with diced onion, cilantro, salsa and lime wedges.
tips: Use two sheet pans if the pork is piled up. Crowded meat steams instead of crisping.
Skim the fat off the leftover juices and save them. Spoon a little over leftovers before reheating so they stay juicy.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freezer up to 3 months, with some of the juices. Reheat in a hot skillet over medium-high heat 3–5 min, until sizzling and crisp at the edges.
